name: Cordyceps
description: Parasitic fungus that chemically hijacks host nervous systems via targeted alkaloids. Manipulates specific neural pathways while keeping host alive. Fruiting body emergence precisely timed to optimal spore dispersal conditions.

core_attributes.pattern: neurochemical hijacking, behavioral parasitism, precision-timed fruiting

scope.definition: Behavioral manipulation specificity of Ophiocordyceps unilateralis — proportion of infected carpenter ant hosts that perform species-specific 'summit disease' behavior (climbing then biting at optimal height/substrate) compared to random-location death.

evidence.source: Hughes et al. (2011) 'Behavioral mechanisms and morphological symptoms of zombie ants dying from a fungal infection', BMC Ecology 11:13; de Bekker et al. (2014) chemical ecology of Ophiocordyceps.
cross_domain_examples: >85% of infected ants die biting at 25 cm height on NNW-facing leaves — species-specific optimal humidity
fungal alkaloids (guanidinobutyric acid, sphingosine) identified as behavioral manipulation compounds
Toxoplasma gondii: analogous targeted host behavior modification (rodent fear reduction toward cats)

scope.falsifiability: If infected ants die in random locations (not consistently at 25 cm NNW-facing substrate), the specificity of behavioral manipulation is not operating and infection outcome is non-deterministic.
scope.measurement_limits: Specificity is species-pair-dependent — each Ophiocordyceps strain targets one host ant species. Manipulation fails at temperatures >30°C. Behavioral specificity is weaker in lab vs field conditions.
